_readme: Content for the five process slides (deck slides 14-18). Edit text here, then run: python3 deck-src/build.py. pins: attribute number -> {el: id of the element in the screen HTML, t: tooltip title, b: tooltip body}. Process 1 pins are grouped per role tab. captions: line shown above the screen for each state (processes 2-5).

processes.speaker_notes: Define the role. One product can be an assistant, a coach and a collaborator — as long as each one is obvious. Four things make the role obvious. It explains itself at first use. It uses a pattern people already know — a big search box. It starts with useful defaults, so there is no blank box. And it shows the well-lit path: every task arrives with its guided next actions, and the person chooses to take them.

1.b: Before any work starts, it says what you can ask and how it helps, in plain language.

2.b: A search box everyone knows. Ask in your own words; chips show which sources it reads.

3.b: Useful questions are ready below the ask box, so there is never a blank start.

1.b: The coach opens on the record you are looking at, with the AI mark, and talks about that record only.

2.b: Name and status first: the same summary card people already use.

3.b: An AI summary is already on the card, so there is no blank start.

4.b: Each task comes with its AI actions ready. The coach points to the right next step, and you choose to take it.

1.b: Three agents are shown up front, and each owns one part of the job.

2.b: Counts first, like any dashboard. Nothing new to learn.

3.b: The first answer is a ready summary: what was found, split into ready, needs review and blocked.

4.b: Every item arrives with its actions: approve or edit. The path forward is lit, and the person takes it.

processes.speaker_notes: Expose capabilities and limits. It shows how it decided and how sure it is, and says it can make mistakes. It lets you start with one item instead of everything at once. It asks before it reads your data, and says why. And it explains only what affects the decision: three checks, one result.

1.t: How it decided, how sure it is
1.b: Sources it evaluated, a short summary, its confidence as a gauge, and the three reasons behind the match.

2.b: Each item has its own approve. Nobody has to say yes to all of it at once.

3.b: It names the data and says why it needs each one. Allow, choose the data, or not now.

4.b: Three checks, shown plainly. No model details, only what is needed to decide.

captions.1: Quick action: how it decided, and how sure it is.
captions.2: Review: try it on one item before all.
captions.3: Before it starts, it asks for your OK.
captions.4: Result: only what affects the decision.

processes.speaker_notes: Choose trust principles. For this product: transparency, control and proof. Before any summary it lists the six sources it fetched. Every number opens into the records behind it. Nothing changes until a person approves. And the outside file is marked as an outside source.

1.b: Every source it fetched is listed before the summary, with what each one was used for.

2.b: The details button opens the records behind the number, so anyone can verify it.

3.b: Approve or leave it. Nothing changes until a person says so.

4.b: The outside file comes from outside the system, and it is marked that way.

captions.1: It fetches the sources, then gives the summary.

processes.speaker_notes: Localize behavior and tone. One agent, three contexts, three different recommendations — and the stakes in each context decide how strong the advice is and how much it explains. New people get meaning and guidance; experts get one line and a bulk action. And work moves across slowly: high touch, low touch, zero touch. High-stakes work stays with people.

1.b: One agent, three clients. It looks at each context and how it runs, then recommends, with the reason beside it.

2.b: High stakes means more checks and more reasons. Low stakes gets one line and a quick action.

3.b: Someone new gets meaning and guidance. An expert gets one line and a bulk action.

4.b: Tasks move from you decide, to you confirm, to handled for you as trust grows. High-stakes work stays with people.

captions.1: One agent, three clients, three answers.
captions.3: The same issue, explained two ways.
captions.4: Trust is earned one task at a time.

processes.speaker_notes: Measure both directions. Size the error first — five questions decide how loudly to warn. Let people say no, with a reason. When something fails, it admits it and marks the numbers as possibly old. Then it gives a way back, with a person in the path, and it learns.

1.b: Five questions decide how loudly to warn, and who needs to know.

2.b: A reason is required on a no, and people can ask for another match in the same step.

3.b: It admits the failure, and says the numbers may be old.

4.b: Retry, explain or call a person. It also learns, so the same failure is caught sooner.

captions.1: How bad could this mistake be?
